name: Slovenia
summary: Slovenia taxes capital gains and dividends at 25%. The capital gains rate falls to 20% after 5 years, 15% after 10 and 0% after 15 years of holding. Children are fully exempt from inheritance and gift tax, and there is no wealth tax. No special regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation of residents; capital income taxed separately at schedular rates as a final tax.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident under the permanent residence, habitual abode, centre of vital interests or 183-day tests.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares, bonds, fund units and real estate are taxed at a flat 25% final tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2), reduced by holding period: 20% after 5 years, 15% after 10 years, and exempt after 15 years. Applies to domestic and foreign assets alike.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt after 15 years of holding (20 years until 31 Dec 2021). Main home exempt if owned, registered as permanent residence and actually lived in for the last 3 years. Gains inside an individual investment account (INR, from 5 Mar 2026) are taxed only on withdrawal at 15%, and the first withdrawal after 15 years is exempt; contributions are capped (EUR 20,000 in year one, then EUR 5,000/yr plus EUR 5,000 for Slovenian instruments, EUR 150,000 lifetime), so INR is immaterial for a large portfolio.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Holding period counted per lot under FIFO (Art. 103 ZDoh-2). Losses offset only capital gains of the same year; a 30-day wash-sale rule disallows losses where identical securities are bought 30 days before or after.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: A gift of capital is a disposal for the donor, but for gifts to a spouse or child the gain can be deferred to the recipient's later sale (application within 15 days). Inheritance is not a disposal. Derivatives are taxed under a separate tax on gains from derivative instruments.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Rates shown assume holding beyond 15 years (0%). Shorter holdings: 25% (0–5 years), 20% (5–10), 15% (10–15). An actively rebalanced portfolio will realise most gains at 25%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: If securities trading is carried on as a business activity, the income becomes business income under the progressive scale (top bracket 45% or 50% depending on the year, per the FURS guide; not verified for 2026) instead of capital gains; private investing is normally treated as capital gains.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 25% → 20% after 5 years → 15% after 10 years → 0% after 15 years; FIFO per identical security.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains; foreign tax paid can be credited. Must self-report gains on foreign brokers (annual return by 28 Feb).
open_questions: No deemed-disposal exit tax for individuals is described in the FURS 2026 capital income guide; not checked against the full ZDoh-2 text.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 25% final tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2), with no holding-period reduction. Foreign dividends are taxed at 25% with a credit for foreign withholding tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 1,000 annual exemption applies only to interest on bank deposits with Slovenian/EU banks, not to dividends. INR account dividends are taxed only on withdrawal (15%).

dividends.rate_basis: Flat 25% final tax on gross dividend; foreign withholding credited (normally limited to the treaty rate).
dividends.withholding_outbound: PwC: standard 15% WHT on dividends paid to non-residents (0% to qualifying EU parent companies; treaty rates 0–15%). Dividends to individuals are subject to the 25% schedular tax.
dividends.treaty_network: 59 treaties in force (PwC), including the US, all major EU states, UK and Switzerland.

wealth_tax.summary: Slovenia has no net wealth tax and no annual levy on financial assets.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipalities levy a building-land use charge (NUSZ) on real estate. No general national real property tax was found to be in force for 2026 (not verified).

open_questions: Status of any national real estate tax proposal not verified (search budget exhausted).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax (ZDDD) is levied on the recipient, but children, adopted children and their descendants, spouse and unmarried partner (first inheritance order) are fully exempt, for both inheritances and gifts.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: First-order exemption (Art. 9 ZDDD) also covers sons/daughters-in-law and stepchildren. Other heirs: movables-only transfers below EUR 5,000 exempt.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Rates for non-exempt recipients (Art. 8): 5%–14% (parents, siblings), 8%–17% (grandparents), 12%–39% (others). A lifetime gift of shares or real estate is a capital-gains disposal for the parent unless deferral to the child is claimed (see capital gains).

inheritance.gift_tax: Same tax as inheritance; gifts to children are exempt. Gifts must be declared within 15 days.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Applies to property received by Slovenian residents, including foreign assets; children exempt regardless.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Liability attaches to the recipient's residence or the location of Slovenian property; no tail rules found.
inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse and unmarried (extramarital) partner of the deceased are first-order heirs, fully exempt from inheritance and gift tax (ZDDD Art. 9; FURS).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a registered permanent residence, a habitual abode, a centre of personal and economic interests in Slovenia, or is present more than 183 days in a tax year (PwC).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.requirements: Register residence for stays over 3 months; no investment requirement.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit
routes.requirements: Permit for a purpose such as employment, business/self-employment or family reunification; no investor-visa route found (not verified).

corporate.summary: CIT is 22% for 2024–2028 (temporarily raised from 19%). Participation-exemption details not verified here.

us_citizen_notes: US–Slovenia income tax treaty in force (2001). US citizens still file US returns; Slovenian 25% tax on capital income is creditable against US tax on foreign-source income.
open_questions: ZIURS (adopted 11 May 2026) cut rental income tax from 25% to 15% (5% for some long-term lets) retroactive to 2026 (Forvis Mazars); its referendum status was reported as contested in Aug 2026 (not verified). No change to capital gains or dividends was found.
Press headlines in 2026 referred to a ministry proposal on capital gains (30% for 5 years, 0 after 20 years) later abandoned; not verified.
Rent based on 3-5 listings only; BISL 2026-27 fees not found; purchase price, health insurance and housekeeper costs not sourced.
